title: Plant Growth and Development
syllabus: Seed germination; Phases of plant growth and plant growth rate; Conditions of growth; Differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; Sequence of developmental process in a plant cell; Plant growth regulators - Auxin, Gibberellin, Cytokinin, Ethylene, and Abscisic acid (ABA).

questions.question: Which of the following scientists first isolated and crystallized Auxin from human urine?
questions.solution: Auxins (from Greek 'auxein': to grow) were first isolated from human urine by Kögl and Haagen-Smit (1931). F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings (Avena coleoptile curvature test).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the discovery of Plant Growth Regulators (PGRs) and their associated experimental systems:

List-I (Scientist)List-II (Discovery / Experimental Material)
(A) Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin(I) 'Bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease in rice caused by Gibberella fujikuroi
(B) E. Kurosawa(II) Phototropism and unilateral curvature of canary grass (Phalaris) coleoptiles
(C) F. Skoog and Carlos Miller(III) Volatile substance from ripened oranges promoting ripening of bananas (Ethylene)
(D) H.H. Cousins(IV) Crystallised cytokinesis-promoting active substance 'Kinetin' from autoclaved herring sperm DNA

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Darwins: Phototropism in canary grass coleoptiles (auxin); E. Kurosawa: Bakanae disease in rice (gibberellins); Skoog & Miller: Kinetin from herring sperm DNA (cytokinins); Cousins: Volatile ripening substance (ethylene).

questions.question: The geometric growth phase showing an S-shaped sigmoid curve is expressed by the mathematical equation $W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$. In this equation, '$r$' represents:
options: Relative growth rate and the measure of the ability of the plant to produce new material (efficiency index)
Initial base constant with zero dimension
questions.solution: In $W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}$, $W_1 = \text{final size}$, $W_0 = \text{initial size}$, $r = \text{relative growth rate}$ (also called the efficiency index, which is the measure of the ability of the plant to generate new plant material), $t = \text{time}$, and $e = \text{base of natural logarithms}$.

questions.question: Formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium (phellogen) from fully differentiated parenchymatous cells is an example of:
questions.solution: Dedifferentiation is the biological process where living, mature, differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide regain the power of mitotic division under specific conditions (e.g., formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from cortical/medullary parenchyma).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the physiological roles of Auxins in agriculture and horticulture:

List-I (Application)List-II (Auxin / Physiological Mechanism)
(A) Selective eradication of broad-leaved dicot weeds(I) 2,4-D (2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid)
(B) Rooting of stem cuttings in plant propagation(II) Indole-3-butyric acid (IBA) / NAA
(C) Apical dominance(III) Decapitation (removal of shoot tips) stimulates lateral bud growth (e.g., tea plantations)
(D) Induction of parthenocarpy(IV) Application to unpollinated ovaries in tomatoes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 2,4-D is used as a selective herbicide to kill broad-leaved dicot weeds in cereal monocot fields; IBA/NAA promote root initiation in stem cuttings; Decapitation breaks apical dominance; Auxins induce seedless fruits (parthenocarpy) in tomatoes.

questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators is an adenine (purine) derivative called $N^6$-furfurylamino purine?
questions.solution: Kinetin (a cytokinin) is a modified adenine base ($N^6$-furfurylamino purine) discovered by Skoog and Miller from autoclaved DNA of herring sperm.

questions.question: Bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering in rosette plants like cabbage and beet) can be induced artificially by the application of:
questions.solution: Gibberellins promote internode elongation just prior to flowering in plants with rosette habits (such as beet, cabbage, and many biennials); this phenomenon is called bolting.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the hormone Ethylene:
Statement I: Ethylene promotes horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis, and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings (triple response).
Statement II: Ethylene induces rapid internode and petiole elongation in deep-water rice plants to keep the upper foliage above water.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Ethylene causes the classic triple response in dicot seedlings and accelerates petiole/internode elongation in submerged deep-water rice plants.

questions.question: Which plant hormone acts as a general plant growth inhibitor, promotes stomatal closure during water stress, and induces seed dormancy?
questions.solution: Abscisic acid (ABA) stimulates stomatal closure during desiccation/water stress (earning the name 'stress hormone'), inhibits seed germination, and promotes seed dormancy, acting as an antagonist to gibberellins.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the bioassays used for detecting plant hormones:

List-I (PGR)List-II (Specific Bioassay)
(A) Auxin(I) $\alpha$-Amylase induction bioassay in barley endosperm
(B) Gibberellin(II) Avena coleoptile curvature test
(C) Cytokinin(III) Triple response test in pea seedlings / Fruit ripening assay
(D) Ethylene(IV) Delay of leaf senescence (Richmond-Lang effect) / Tobacco callus test

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Auxin: Avena curvature test; Gibberellin: $\alpha$-Amylase production in germinating barley; Cytokinin: Tobacco pith callus cell division and delay of chlorophyll degradation (Richmond-Lang effect); Ethylene: Triple response in etiolated seedlings.

questions.question: Plasticity in plant growth refers to the ability of a plant to:
options: Follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures (e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur)
Regenerate complete organs from isolated protoplasts
Grow in length by elongation of apical meristems only
questions.solution: Plants follow different developmental pathways in response to environmental cues or during different life phases to produce distinct structures; this capability is called plasticity (e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander, larkspur, and buttercup).

questions.question: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, which of the following patterns of daughter cell fate occurs?
options: Only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures ($L_t = L_0 + rt$)
Both daughter cells retain the ability to divide continuously
Both daughter cells immediately lose dividing power and die
Cells divide only in three planes forming a sphere
questions.solution: In arithmetic growth, only one daughter cell continues to divide at a constant rate while the other differentiates and matures, producing a linear growth curve mathematically expressed as $L_t = L_0 + rt$ (e.g., root elongation at constant rate).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the cellular characteristics in the three phases of root/stem growth:

List-I (Phase of Growth)List-II (Cellular Characteristics)
(A) Meristematic phase(I) Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition
(B) Elongation phase(II) Maximal wall thickening, structural differentiation, and functional maturity
(C) Maturation phase(III) Rich in protoplasm, large prominent nuclei, thin cellulosic primary walls with abundant plasmodesmata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Meristematic zone: Cells have dense protoplasm, large nuclei, and thin primary walls; Elongation zone: Characterized by rapid vacuolation and cell expansion; Maturation zone: Cells attain maximal size and undergo secondary thickening and differentiation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a naturally occurring plant cytokinin isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk?
questions.solution: Zeatin is a natural cytokinin first isolated from immature corn kernels (Zea mays) by Letham. (Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants; it was discovered from autoclaved animal DNA).

questions.question: Spraying juvenile conifers with which of the following PGRs hastens the maturity period, leading to early seed production?
questions.solution: Application of gibberellins to juvenile conifers hastens the maturity period and shortens the life cycle, leading to early cone and seed production.

questions.question: Ethephon is the most widely used source of ethylene in agriculture because it is:
options: An aqueous compound that is readily absorbed, translocated, and slowly releases ethylene inside plant tissues
A solid powder that absorbs atmospheric oxygen
A gas stored under high pressure cylinders
A synthetic competitive inhibitor of auxin
questions.solution: Ethephon is an aqueous formulation (2-chloroethylphosphonic acid) that is readily absorbed and translocated within the plant, where it slowly hydrolyzes and releases ethylene gas at neutral or basic physiological pH.

questions.question: Secondary cortex (phelloderm) and cork (phellem) formed by the activity of cork cambium (phellogen) are examples of:
questions.solution: Redifferentiation occurs when dedifferentiated meristematic cells (like cork cambium or vascular cambium) divide and lose their dividing capacity again to form specialized mature permanent tissues (e.g., secondary xylem, secondary phloem, phelloderm, and cork).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the chemical nature and classifications of Plant Growth Regulators:

List-I (PGR)List-II (Chemical Nature)
(A) Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA)(I) Carotenoid derivative / Sesquiterpene
(B) Gibberellic acid ($\text{GA}_3$)(II) Gaseous hydrocarbon
(C) Abscisic acid (ABA)(III) Terpenes (Diterpenoid)
(D) Ethylene(IV) Indole derivatives

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: IAA/IBA: Indole derivatives; GAs: Terpenes/diterpenoids; Cytokinins: Adenine derivatives; ABA: Carotenoid derivative; Ethylene: Gaseous hydrocarbon.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations of hormones is added to culture media in plant tissue culture to regulate organogenesis (shoot and root regeneration)?
questions.solution: Skoog and Miller demonstrated that the ratio of Auxin to Cytokinin controls morphogenesis in callus: High auxin/cytokinin ratio promotes rhizogenesis (roots); High cytokinin/auxin ratio promotes caulogenesis (shoots); Intermediate balanced ratio promotes undifferentiated callus proliferation.

questions.question: Spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thereby increasing the crop yield by as much as:
questions.solution: Sugarcane stores carbohydrates as sugar in stems. Spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, increasing yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre.

questions.question: Which of the following plant hormones is synthesized in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits?
questions.solution: Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR synthesized in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and by ripening fruits, where it induces a respiratory climacteric (sharp rise in respiration rate).

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the sequence of developmental processes in a plant cell:
Statement I: Development is the sum total of two biological processes: Growth and Differentiation.
Statement II: The correct developmental sequence is: Meristematic cell $\to$ Plasmatic growth $\to$ Cell division $\to$ Expansion $\to$ Maturation $\to$ Senescence $\to$ Death.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Development includes all changes an organism goes through during its life cycle from seed germination to senescence. Development = Growth + Differentiation.

questions.question: Apical dominance (inhibition of lateral axillary bud growth by the apical shoot tip) is mediated predominantly by:
questions.solution: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance, caused by polar basipetal transport of auxins.

questions.question: Which of the following PGRs can overcome apical dominance and promote the outgrowth of lateral branches and bushy growth?
questions.solution: Cytokinins counteract apical dominance by promoting nutrient mobilization and lateral bud growth, making plants bushier.

questions.question: The respiratory climacteric (sudden sharp rise in the rate of cellular respiration during fruit ripening) is triggered by:
questions.solution: Ethylene enhances the respiration rate during ripening of fruits (such as apples, bananas, and tomatoes). This dramatic metabolic rise is called the respiratory climacteric.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the physiological roles of Gibberellins:

List-I (Effect / Application)List-II (Crop / Plant System)
(A) Elongation of stalks to improve cluster shape(I) Apples (elongation and shape improvement)
(B) Delay of fruit senescence(II) Grapes
(C) Speeding up malting process(III) Brewing industry (barley grains)
(D) Improvement of fruit shape and size(IV) Citrus fruits (extended tree-holding period)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Grapes: Stalk elongation; Citrus: Delay of senescence allowing fruits to stay on trees longer; Brewing: $\text{GA}_3$ accelerates malting; Apples: Improvement of length and market shape.

questions.question: Abscisic acid (ABA) is referred to as an antagonist to which of the following plant hormones?
questions.solution: ABA acts as an antagonist to gibberellins (GAs). While GAs stimulate seed germination, mobilization of endosperm reserves, and flowering, ABA promotes seed dormancy, prevents precocious viviparous germination, and inhibits growth.

questions.question: During the differentiation of tracheary elements (vessels and tracheids), the cells undergo which structural changes?
options: Loss of their living protoplasm and development of very strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls
Excessive accumulation of dense cytoplasm and loss of cell walls
Rapid continuous mitotic division without wall thickening
Deposition of waxy suberin only on outer tangential walls
questions.solution: To form tracheary xylem elements, cells lose their entire living protoplasm (become dead at maturity) and develop very strong, rigid, lignocellulosic secondary cell wall thickenings to withstand high tensile negative pressure during water conduction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a synthetic auxin widely used as a selective weedicide and herbicide?
questions.solution: 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) and 2,4,5-T are synthetic auxins. 2,4-D is widely used as a weedicide to clear dicot weeds in lawns and monocot cereal plantations.

questions.question: Environmental heterophylly (development of different leaf forms in response to air versus water environments) is prominently exhibited by:
questions.solution: In Ranunculus (buttercup), the leaves emerging in air are broad and lobed, whereas submerged leaves in water are finely dissected. This is an example of environmental plasticity/heterophylly.

questions.question: Thinning of excess cotton, cherry, and walnut fruits is commercially achieved by the application of:
questions.solution: Ethephon promotes abscission of flowers and fruits; thus, it is used commercially for thinning of excess fruits in cotton, cherry, and walnut.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is NOT an essential requirement for normal plant growth?
options: Continuous supply of green light only
Water for cell turgidity and enzymatic medium
questions.solution: Essential requirements for plant growth include water (for turgor-driven cell enlargement), oxygen (for aerobic ATP generation), essential macro- and micro-nutrients, and an optimal temperature range ($20-35^\circ\text{C}$). Green light is mostly reflected by plants.

questions.question: Richmond-Lang effect refers to the delay of leaf senescence and chlorophyll degradation by the application of:
questions.solution: Cytokinins delay natural senescence in leaves by promoting active nutrient mobilization and preventing the breakdown of proteins and chlorophyll (known as the Richmond-Lang effect).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of growth measurement parameters:

List-I (Plant Tissue / System)List-II (Measurement Parameter of Growth)
(A) Maize root apical meristem(I) Increase in surface area
(B) Watermelon fruit cell(II) Increase in cell number (up to 17,500 new cells per hour)
(C) Dorsiventral leaf(III) Increase in cell volume (up to 350,000 times)
(D) Pollen tube(IV) Growth measured in terms of length

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Maize root tip: Number of cells ($17,500/\text{hr}$); Watermelon cell: Cell volume ($350,000\times$); Leaf: Surface area; Pollen tube: Length.

questions.question: The precursor amino acid for the biological synthesis of natural auxin (Indole-3-acetic acid / IAA) in plant tissues is:
questions.solution: The essential aromatic amino acid Tryptophan serves as the biochemical precursor for the biosynthesis of IAA in plants, requiring Zinc ($\text{Zn}^{2+}$) as an enzyme activator.

questions.question: Which of the following amino acids acts as the primary biochemical precursor for the gaseous plant hormone Ethylene?
questions.solution: The sulfur-containing amino acid Methionine (via S-adenosylmethionine / SAM and ACC pathways) is the precursor for ethylene biosynthesis.

questions.question: Promotion of female flowers (feminizing effect) in cucumbers is commercially accomplished using:
questions.solution: Ethylene promotes female flowers in cucumbers, increasing the number of fruits and overall commercial crop yield.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Auxins prevent fruit and leaf drop at early young stages, but promote the abscission of older, mature leaves and fruits.
Statement II: IBA and NAA are synthetic and natural auxins used extensively in tea plantations and stem cuttings.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Auxins prevent premature abscission of young leaves and fruits, but accelerate the shedding (abscission) of older mature organs.

questions.question: In a sigmoid growth curve, the three successive growth phases observed are:
options: Lag phase, Log (exponential) phase, and Stationary phase
Log phase, Lag phase, and Linear phase
Linear phase, Exponential phase, and Death phase
Stationary phase, Lag phase, and Log phase
questions.solution: A typical sigmoid growth curve comprises: (1) an initial slow Lag phase, (2) a rapid exponential Log phase, and (3) a final slowing Stationary phase due to limited nutrient availability.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of dedifferentiated tissue in plants?
options: Interfascicular cambium, cork cambium, and wound meristem
questions.solution: Interfascicular cambium, cork cambium (phellogen), and wound cambium are secondary meristems formed by the dedifferentiation of fully mature parenchymatous cells.

questions.question: The hormone that promotes rapid cell division in the presence of auxins, stimulates chloroplast development in leaves, and promotes adventitious shoot formation is:
questions.solution: Cytokinins promote cytokinesis (cell division), formation of new leaves and chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth, and adventitious shoot formation.

questions.question: In seeds of barley and wheat, the hydrolysis of endosperm starch into maltose and glucose during germination is triggered by the secretion of $\alpha$-amylase induced by:
questions.solution: During cereal seed germination, gibberellin ($	ext{GA}_3$) released from the embryo diffuses into the aleurone layer, activating genes for hydrolytic enzymes (such as $\alpha$-amylase and proteases) that break down endosperm reserves for the growing seedling.

questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, and promotes sprouting of potato tubers?
questions.solution: Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates sprouting of potato tubers, and accelerates germination in peanut seeds.

questions.question: Plant growth is generally unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout life. This open form of growth is due to the presence of:
options: Meristems at specific locations in their body
Lignified dead tissues throughout the stem
Permanent vascular bundles with closed cambium
questions.solution: Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited indeterminate growth throughout their lifespan. This 'open form of growth' is due to the presence of localized dividing cells called meristems.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the primary source sites of Plant Growth Regulators in plants:

List-I (PGR)List-II (Primary Site of Synthesis)
(A) Auxin(I) Root apices and developing shoot buds
(B) Gibberellin(II) Growing apices of shoots and roots
(C) Cytokinin(III) Young leaves, shoot apices, and developing seeds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Auxins are produced primarily in growing shoot and root apices; Gibberellins are synthesized in young leaves, shoot apices, and developing seeds; Cytokinins are synthesized in regions of rapid cell division, primarily root apices, shoot buds, and young developing fruits.
